system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Gating points:** No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap, the 18-month claims period, or a post-Completion Riverlark release. Until she gives it, we should counter at our starting positions.

| ID | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m aggregate for general Warranty Claims (cl. 12.1). | 25% / AUD 6.0m starting position. 20% / AUD 4.8m only as a conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; counter at AUD 6.0m.** The AUD 4.8m figure is a fallback we cannot offer without written principal authority. |
| **SPA-N-002** De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl. 12.2). | De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject.** Five-times thresholds with excess-only recovery would strip out most small and mid-size claims. |
| **SPA-N-003** General claims time limit | 18 months after Completion for general claims (cl. 12.3/13). Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | 24 months after Completion. 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Reject the "applies to all Claims" default. | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** The blanket default would pull Title, Fraud and other categories into the general limits. |
| **SPA-N-004** Fundamental / Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties (cl. 12 "administrative simplicity"). | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject.** Title to the shares is our core ownership protection and cannot sit under a 20% cap. |
| **SPA-N-005** Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent. Non-waivable. | **Reject; insert the carve-out.** "Any nature" wording would capture fraud, which the playbook excludes from every limitation. |
| **SPA-N-006** Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the whole data room (to 5.00pm 22 Sep 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1, 1.2; Sch 7). | Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2; accept specific disclosures only.** Deemed disclosure of the data room would defeat warranty claims for matters we never specifically saw. |
| **SPA-N-007** Buyer knowledge qualifier | Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3). | Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Delete cl. 8.3.** A "discoverable" bar is a constructive-knowledge test that would swallow the warranties after our due diligence. |
| **SPA-N-008** Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl. 3 / 6.3). DL 2: no final consent or evidence that conditions are met. Revenue ~AUD 3.6m (~30%). | Effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. | **Reject; make it a condition precedent.** The consent covers roughly 30% of revenue and must be effective before we pay. |
| **SPA-N-009** Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2 / 7). DL 3: not repaid, no discharge included. | Current payout figure. Direct repayment from Completion funds. Effective security releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. | **Reject the post-Completion release; require payout from the funds flow.** Leaving a AUD 3.2m secured facility in place exposes the company we are buying to the lender's security. |
| **SPA-N-010** Employee bonuses | Matter for the Seller. Not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5: AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses, on-costs unstated. | DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item, or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **Require a specific line item or Seller funding.** Unscheduled bonuses plus on-costs would pass to us as post-Completion leakage. |
| **SPA-N-011** Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl. 11.1). DL 4: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010, not bank-verified; transfer conditional on cleared payment (DD-004 cl. 7.3); no receipt or assignment on file. | Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. | **Broaden the indemnity; do not accept "adequate."** A payment-only indemnity does not cover transfer failure of the SOW3 Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012** Export / privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6 / Sch 6). DL 6: ~1,240 records possibly exported; access, scope and notification unresolved. | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. | **Do not accept or reject materiality; require preservation, investigation and regular updates.** Access and scope are unknown, so neither party's characterisation is established. |
| **SPA-N-013** Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, described as ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8: unavoidability, termination rights and accrual not stated. | Assess each renewal. No automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction. | **Assess before agreeing; no automatic price adjustment.** The "ordinary course" label is unsupported by the record and needs review. |
| **SPA-N-014** Category separation | Tax and IP "settled under the general regime above" (cl. statement re Tax/IP). | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Reject.** Folding categories into the general regime would override the separate Title and Tax/IP protections. |
| **SPA-N-015** Title verification | Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 (Seller's stated position). DL 10: register identifies the source relied on; no Buyer verification stated. | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (for example, independent registry and PPSR searches and confirmation of authority). DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent evidence.** A seller-supplied register is not independent proof of ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016** Tax / IP open terms | Tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general regime. | Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **Do not accept as settled; keep open pending negotiation.** The Seller's label is not agreement, and the playbook treats these terms as unresolved. |
=== END ADVICE ===
